diagnostics.message: :resource.null_resource.wait_for_cluster: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

null_resource.wait_for_cluster has an explicit depends_on on aws_eks_cluster.this, but the dependency is already established implicitly: the local-exec provisioner's environment block references aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint (ENDPOINT), which Terraform uses to order the resource. The explicit depends_on entry is redundant and can be removed; only the depends_on on aws_security_group_rule.cluster_private_access carries unique ordering information.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers launches EC2 instances that use aws_iam_role.workers, but there is no attribute reference or depends_on ordering it after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy (nor the CNI/ECR attachments). If the ASG is created and starts launching instances before the worker role's policies are attached, the nodes boot with a role lacking the required EKS policies and fail to join/operate until IAM propagation catches up. The module already protects the managed node_groups path against exactly this race via the data.null_data_source.node_groups ordering hack (its inputs include the three policy attachment IDs), but the launch-configuration worker group has no equivalent guard. A bare depends_on covering the three worker policy attachments closes the gap; there is no clean data reference on the ASG that would express it.
